clue.text: Messy sort runs when brush is around

indicators.note: the word for brush is said to surround the abbreviation, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: to scuff is to brush or scrape lightly against something
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An untidy character dashes off whenever a hairbrush is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is an informal noun for a shabby, unkempt person.

clue.text: Lowering small engine cover

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a cowling is the removable metal casing over an aircraft engine

explanation.surface: Bringing down a little hood over a motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowering' looks like letting something down; it is the other word, pronounced to rhyme with 'flowering', meaning frowning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowering, said to rhyme with flowering, means glowering or frowning sullenly.

clue.text: Cooker is new being in fashion

indicators.note: being in means the letter for new is placed inside the word for fashion

parts.note: the rage is the current fashion

explanation.surface: A novel stove is now trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large kitchen stove with ovens and hotplates.

clue.text: Shabby cinema to furnish around spring

indicators.note: around means the word for furnish encloses the word for spring

parts.note: to fit out or fit is to furnish or equip
a leap is a spring or jump

explanation.surface: Kitting out a run-down picture house in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleapit is British slang for a dingy, run-down cinema or theatre.

clue.text: A detective force in charge is sharp

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: A police detective unit with responsibility is described as keen-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic tastes or remarks are tart and biting, both senses of sharp.

clue.text: Man attending Indian's first served this

definitions.text: Man attending Indian's first served this

parts.note: a chap is a man
at means present at, attending

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word Indian

explanation.surface: A fellow at an Indian restaurant was given this to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened flatbread served with Indian meals.

clue.text: Knightly adventure going wrong in strange upset

indicators.note: in means the word for going wrong sits inside the other piece
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: odd means strange
erring means making a mistake, going wrong

explanation.surface: A chivalrous quest goes awry in a peculiar overturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the word for strange upside down, and the word for going wrong sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is heroic, daring action of the sort found in tales of chivalry.

clue.text: Man left in social group

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for social group

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class

explanation.surface: A fellow abandoned within his class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person; it is a chess man, a piece on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess any piece is called a man, and the rook is also called by this name.

clue.text: Wood that can make wind instrument and timber

parts.note: a horn is a brass instrument played by blowing
a beam is a long piece of timber

explanation.surface: A material from which one could fashion both a horn and a building beam.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornbeam is a hardwood tree whose tough timber is prized by woodworkers.

clue.text: Somehow mind big rock singer copying others

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unspecified new arrangement

explanation.surface: A big rock vocalist, oddly enough, imitates other performers.
explanation.definitionFit: The mockingbird is a songbird known for mimicking the calls of other birds.

clue.text: A sign of ignorance like this clue!

parts.note: someone unable to write signs a document with a cross mark instead of a name

explanation.surface: A mark made by an unlettered person describes the very clue in front of you.
explanation.definitionFit: This clue sits among the horizontal entries of the grid, so it is a horizontal one.

clue.text: Run away fast taking short cut

indicators.note: the word for fast is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: fleet means swift or fast

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off quickly by taking a shortcut.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to escape or bolt from danger.

clue.text: I called cop out for minor offence

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone summons the police over a trivial misdemeanour.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a small sin or trivial fault.

clue.text: Hosting internet, gain trolls

indicators.note: trolls, read as a verb meaning wander about, tells us to shuffle the preceding letters

explanation.surface: Running a web service attracts online troublemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertaining guests means hosting them, offering hospitality.

clue.text: Upcoming fashion designer wearing something hot and elaborate

indicators.note: the designer wears the hot thing, so it is clothed by it, going inside

parts.note: an ember is a glowing piece of coal or wood

indicators.note: upcoming in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: Christian Dior was a famous French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A rising couturier dressed in something sizzling and ornate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming' reads the designer's name upwards in this down clue; 'wearing' puts it inside the hot thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider a story is to elaborate it with invented detail.

clue.text: Commemorate sapper apparently

definitions.meaning: to commemorate is to honour the memory of, to recall
a sapper is a soldier of the Royal Engineers, RE

explanation.surface: Honour a military engineer, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps whose private soldiers are called sappers.
explanation.definitionFit: To commemorate someone is to keep them in mind and honour them.

clue.text: Frustrated diarist could be deserting job

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A thwarted journal-keeper might be walking out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Helen Fielding's comic novel heroine keeps a diary full of romantic and career frustrations.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional heroine of Bridget Jones's Diary is a famously exasperated diary-keeper.

clue.text: Clear up press in print

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
a book that is out has been published and is in print

explanation.surface: Tidy up the printing press.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron out problems is to resolve or settle them.

clue.text: Mug putting armoured vehicle on a little road

parts.note: a tank is an armoured military vehicle
RD is the short form of road

explanation.surface: A drinking vessel placing a military tank on a small lane.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, often pewter with a handle.

clue.text: Surly detective taking over

indicators.note: taking means the detective holds the letter for over inside

parts.note: Inspector Morse is a fictional Oxford detective of novels and television
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A grumpy inspector takes charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means gloomy and sullen, ill-tempered.

clue.text: There's something soothing about crooner for a dance

indicators.note: about means the soothing item goes around the singer

parts.note: a lotion is a soothing cream or liquid
Perry Como was a famous American crooner

explanation.surface: A calming balm is applied to a ballad singer before he dances.
explanation.walkthrough: The Loco-Motion was a 1960s dance craze from the Little Eva song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loco-Motion is a novelty dance popularised by a 1962 hit record.

clue.text: Organised work session with loud complaint

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for communal work, as in a sewing bee
F stands for forte, the musical direction meaning loud

explanation.surface: A planned team meeting comes with a noisy grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is slang for a grievance or grumble.

clue.text: Speculate about the Queen's headgear

indicators.note: about means the word for speculate goes around the royal letters

parts.note: to bet is to gamble or speculate
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Guess about Her Majesty's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a soft, round, flat cap.

clue.text: Gangster ducks source of bad luck

parts.note: hood is short for hoodlum, a gangster
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks look like two zeros, O and O

explanation.surface: A mobster dodges something that brings misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a jinx, a person or thing that brings misfortune.

clue.text: Help to turn race, getting stream of invective

indicators.note: to turn means the word for help is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: aid means help
a tribe is a people or race

explanation.surface: Assistance swings a contest, provoking an angry rant.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter, abusive verbal attack.

clue.text: Wading birds like others, twitching tail

parts.note: eg, for example, means like

indicators.note: the end of the word for others is jerked about, its last two letters swapping places

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Long-legged waterbirds, like their companions, flick their rear feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twitching tail' swaps the final two letters of REST to give RETS. Birdwatchers are 'twitchers', which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white herons that wade in shallow water to feed.

clue.text: Person in charge of columns drove back without it

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the reversed word surrounds the other piece
back means the word for drove is read in reverse

parts.note: rode means travelled, drove

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss took the car back home leaving something behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside; 'back' reads the word for drove in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper editor is responsible for the content of its columns.
